I have been working this land for 45 years, and my father worked it before me. Ten mu is not a big farm, but with six mouths in the house and some of the young ones working in town, it is enough if I manage it carefully.

For wheat this winter, I will plant an improved variety — the seed dealer in town sells good ones from the county station, and my neighbor got over 500 kg last year with it. I sow around mid-October after the maize comes off. I use about 15 kg of seed per mu. For fertilizer, before planting I broadcast diammonium phosphate (二铵) as base — about one 50-kg bag per 3 mu gives me roughly 8 kg P per mu, plus some N. Then in spring at greenup/jointing, I topdress urea, about 15 kg urea per mu, which gives me my nitrogen. Altogether I figure about 16 kg N per mu, which is what most people around here use. Potassium I add a little through compound fertilizer, maybe 6 kg per mu — our soil here is not too short of potash. I irrigate from the well about 3 times: overwintering water, greenup water, and grain-filling water. Pesticide I usually spray twice — once for aphids and once for wheat scab if the weather turns wet at heading. I expect around 480 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to waste. Hybrid seed is standard now — nobody around here uses old varieties for maize. About 2 kg seed per mu. I use rotary tillage or even just direct drill after wheat stubble. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage — total about 17 kg N per mu for maize, it is a hungry crop. Phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 6 kg per mu. Well irrigation maybe 1-2 times depending on the summer rains — last few years I only had to water once. Pesticide for armyworm and borer, usually 2 sprays. I hope for around 550 kg per mu.

I do not plough deep every year — too expensive to hire the tractor. I rotary till for both crops, maybe once every 3-4 years I do a deep plough. My son helps with the harvest when he comes back from the city.
